title: Characterization of the matrix remainder condition
statement: For every Boolean word $x$ and natural number $n$, the following are equivalent. First, for every $j<n^2$, the two bits of $x$ at positions $2n+2+2j$ and $2n+3+2j$ agree, and the bits at positions $2n+2+2n^2$ and $2n+3+2n^2$ are respectively $0$ and $1$. Second, there is a Boolean word $M$ of length $n^2$ such that, for each $i<n^2$, the bits of $x$ at positions $2n+2+2i$ and $2n+3+2i$ both equal the $i$th bit of $M$, and the same final two positions contain $0$ and $1$, respectively. Out-of-range word positions are interpreted as $0$.
